documents.unit: Library research guide, section by Center for Educational Effectiveness
documents.title: Generative AI for Teaching, Research and Learning: Teaching and Learning
documents.summary: A guidance page by the Center for Educational Effectiveness inside a library guide. It tells students to check each instructor's policy, gives five takeaways for students, and points instructors to consultations and example syllabus language. It sets no university-wide rule.
documents.stance_why: The page says 'policies regarding Generative AI may vary from instructor to instructor' and tells students to 'check with their instructors', while giving instructors links to examples; the decision is handed to instructors, so delegates.

units.why: Describes CEE experts offering consultation: 'available to help instructors explore teaching strategies and construct course policies'. Support for instructors setting policy, so P63.
units.anchor: available to help instructors explore teaching strategies and construct course policies pertaining to Generative AI

units.why: States both groups 'should carefully consider the limitations and emerging best practices'. A duty to stay informed about AI developments, so P102 rather than a framework type.
units.anchor: both students and instructors should carefully consider the limitations and emerging best practices

units.why: Says tools 'can be quite useful for personalizing learning experiences and rethinking teaching and instruction', naming benefits without a rule, so P87 rather than P44.
units.anchor: quite useful for personalizing learning experiences and rethinking teaching and instruction

units.why: Students 'should always check with their instructors' about course policy before using AI. P78 (learn the course's rules) fits better than P10 since it is not framed as 'when unsure'.
units.anchor: students should always check with their instructors to understand their particular course policies
units.frag_start: Before using Generative AI to support
units.fit_note: Also implies ask-before-use, which P10 covers, but the text is unconditional rather than 'when unsure'.

units.why: 'policies regarding Generative AI may vary from instructor to instructor' says the decision rests with each instructor, so P04.
units.anchor: policies regarding Generative AI may vary from instructor to instructor
units.frag_start: Keep in mind that policies regarding

units.why: Takeaway 'Generative AI should be used to support and enhance your thinking' keeps the student as the thinker, so P32.
units.anchor: Generative AI should be used to support and enhance your thinking

units.why: 'Always be mindful of the risks and limitations of Generative AI tools' warns of risks without naming any, so P53 (bias, harms) and P31 (output wrong) do not fit.
units.anchor: Always be mindful of the risks and limitations of Generative AI tools
units.uncovered_note: Students are told generally to stay mindful of AI risks and limitations without naming any specific risk.

units.why: 'Engage with Generative AI output critically' tells students to evaluate output rather than accept it, matching P31.
units.anchor: Engage with Generative AI output critically and practice information literacy

units.why: 'Always follow academic integrity guidelines and instructor policies' binds students to existing integrity and course rules; closest is P78.
units.anchor: Always follow academic integrity guidelines and instructor policies regarding Generative AI
units.fit_note: Also points to academic integrity guidelines generally, which P78 does not name.

units.why: 'Practice proper citation practices for Generative AI use' asks students to cite AI use, so P24.
units.anchor: Practice proper citation practices for Generative AI use

units.why: Notes AI 'led to ongoing questions about how to support and protect student learning'; a problem statement with no rule or mechanism, so P41 does not fit.
units.anchor: led to ongoing questions about how to support and protect student learning
units.uncovered_note: Frames AI as having disrupted teaching and raised open questions about protecting student learning, without a rule or a stated mechanism.

units.why: 'scholarly research has only just begun to explore the implications' admits that evidence is thin, nearest P55.
units.anchor: scholarly research has only just begun to explore the implications of Generative AI
units.fit_note: Says evidence is limited rather than that evidence is being collected.

units.why: CEE 'provides a number of resources, events, and consultations related to Generative AI and teaching', which is faculty support, so P63.
units.anchor: provides a number of resources, events, and consultations related to Generative AI and teaching

units.why: Says institutions 'developed preliminary guidance for instructors to develop transparent expectations and policies', pointing to syllabus examples; closest to P09.
units.anchor: preliminary guidance for instructors to develop transparent expectations and policies regarding Generative AI
units.fit_note: Recommends transparent expectations by pointing to examples; it does not require a syllabus statement.

units.why: 'Instructors may benefit from exploring ways to intentionally incorporate AI' encourages instructors to use AI in teaching, so P59.
units.anchor: Instructors may benefit from exploring ways to intentionally incorporate AI
units.fit_note: Also covers incorporating AI into instructional strategies, beyond drafting materials.

units.why: Early scholarship 'has suggested that intentional and critical use of Generative AI can support student learning'; cites evidence of benefit, so P55.
units.anchor: intentional and critical use of Generative AI can support student learning
units.frag_start: early scholarship of teaching and learning
units.fit_note: Cites emerging scholarship rather than describing evidence collection.

notes: Only one included document, a library-guide page by CEE; mostly link lists, so few units.
